steamflow.standard_clause: ISO 5167-2:2003, §5.3.2 Reader–Harris/Gallagher (1998); IS 14615; IAPWS-IF97 Region 2 & Region 4
steamflow.worked_example: Default on-page calibration case (flange-tap orifice, D = 4.026 in CS, d = 2.500 in SS316, dry saturated steam at P1 = 150 psig, ΔP = 100 inH2O) computes mass flow rate = 4002.4 kg/h (8823.8 lb/hr), Cd = 0.60652, Re_D = 879,075, and ε = 0.99307 (walkthrough Step E/F reference case at κ = 1.300 solves 0.9708 kg/s).
assumptions: Steady-state, axisymmetric single-phase (saturated dry/wet or superheated) steam flow in a circular pipe running full.
Sharp-edged concentric orifice plate, ISA 1932/long-radius nozzle, or classical Venturi geometry per ISO 5167 / IS 14615.
Thermal expansion correction from 20 °C reference using linear expansion coefficients for SS316 plate and carbon steel pipe.
Thermodynamic density, viscosity, and enthalpy evaluated from IAPWS-IF97 Region 2 and Region 4 formulations.
limits: Classical Venturi tubes (ISO 5167-4): 50 mm <= D <= 250 mm (machined), 0.30 <= β <= 0.75, Re_D >= 200,000.
Subcritical differential pressure (P2 / P1 > 0.75 recommended for ISO 5167 expansibility factor validity).
steamflow.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

arcflash.standard_clause: IEEE 1584-2018 (empirical arcing-current, incident-energy & enclosure size correction models); NFPA 70E-2024 Sec 130.4 / Table 130.4(E)(b) / Annex D.5; OSHA 1910.269
arcflash.worked_example: Default on-page 0.48 kV three-phase AC VCB switchgear case (Ibf = 25 kA, clearing time t = 100 ms, gap = 32 mm, working distance = 457 mm, typical enclosure) computes arcing current I_arc = 19.39 kA, incident energy E = 4.65 cal/cm², Arc Flash Boundary AFB = 44.4 in (1128 mm), and NFPA PPE Category 2.
assumptions: Three-phase sustained arc fault in open air or standard rectangular metal enclosure (VCB, VCBB, HCB, VOA, HOA geometries).
Incident energy converted from Stoll second-degree burn threshold (1.2 cal/cm²) to determine Arc Flash Boundary.
Fixed protective device clearing time entered by the user at bolted fault current (upstream/downstream variations checked separately).
DC systems above/below 800 V modeled per NFPA 70E Annex D.5 (Stokes, Oppenlander & Doan methods) rather than AC zero-crossing.
limits: IEEE 1584-2018 empirical AC model applies strictly for 208 V to 15 kV nominal system voltage, 50 Hz or 60 Hz.
Bolted fault current Ibf validity: 0.7 kA to 106 kA (208–600 V) and 0.2 kA to 65 kA (601–15,000 V).
Conductor gap bounds: 6.35 mm to 76.2 mm (LV) and 19.05 mm to 254 mm (MV); minimum working distance >= 305 mm (12 in).
Systems > 15 kV AC require OSHA 1910.269 / NESC tables; single-phase AC and DC follow separate engineering methods.
arcflash.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

cable-sizing.standard_clause: IEC 60364-5-52 / BS 7671 (installation method ampacity & derating tables) & IEC 60364-4-43 (adiabatic short-circuit withstand equation); NEC Table 310.15
cable-sizing.worked_example: Default on-page 400 V three-phase continuous copper/PVC single-core Method C case (Ib = 100 A, pf = 0.85, L = 150 m, max 3% drop) recommends a 70 mm² conductor with derated ampacity 200 A and actual voltage drop 7.63 V (1.91%), governed by Ampacity.
assumptions: Balanced steady-state AC or DC load; intermittent duty sized to user-entered RMS-equivalent current (loadFactor = 1.0).
Cable resistance and reactance values drawn from built-in metric table at rated conductor operating temperature (70 °C PVC / 90 °C XLPE).
Overall derating factor applied as product of ambient temperature, circuit grouping, soil thermal resistivity, and burial depth factors.
Equal current sharing assumed across parallel cable runs of identical length, cross-section, and routing.
limits: Valid only for standard metric conductor sizes present in the built-in impedance table (1.5 mm² to 630 mm²; unknown sizes blocked).
240–630 mm² copper impedance entries should be cross-checked against manufacturer datasheets and IEC 60228 Class 2 max DC resistance at 20 °C for critical feeder runs.
Harmonic-rich non-linear loads (triplen neutral currents) and skin/proximity effects above 630 mm² are not automatically derated.
Short-circuit thermal withstand requires user fault current and clearing time inputs within IEC 60364-4-43 adiabatic time limits (<= 5 s).
cable-sizing.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

valve-cv.standard_clause: IEC 60534-2-1 / ISA-75.01.01 (incompressible, compressible & non-Newtonian FR/Y/xT flow sizing equations); IEC 60534-8 (aerodynamic/hydrodynamic noise)
valve-cv.worked_example: Default on-page subcritical water case (Q = 150 GPM, SG = 1.0, P1 = 60 psia, P2 = 45 psia, Pv = 0.5 psia, Pc = 3200 psia, FL = 0.90) computes required valve Cv = 38.73 at ΔP = 15.00 psi (ΔP_choked = 48.21 psi), valve Reynolds number Rev = 439,535, and viscosity factor FR = 1.0000.
assumptions: Steady-state, isothermal flow across a throttling control valve installed without extreme reducer/swage fitting mismatches unless Fp entered.
Known or manufacturer-supplied valve recovery factor FL, style modifier Fd, and gas critical pressure drop ratio xT.
Two-phase flashing/boiling flow approximated via Homogeneous Equilibrium Model (HEM) assuming zero slip between liquid and vapor phases.
limits: Liquid sizing applies fixed FL across cavitation onset; severe flashing/cavitation trim requires multi-stage verification.
Viscous liquid Reynolds correction factor FR relies on iterative turbulent/transitional/laminar curve fit (valid within ISA-75.01 Rev bounds).
Pipe fitting factor Fp defaults to 1.0 when line size equals valve nominal size; large reducer ratios require explicit Fp adjustment.
valve-cv.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

pump-head.standard_clause: ANSI/HI 14.3 (piping friction & NPSHa analysis); API Standard 610 (NPSH safety margin); ASME B31.3; ISO 9906; IS 15225
pump-head.worked_example: Default on-page 20 °C water case (Q = 18 m³/h, 60 mm suction pipe 10 m long, 50 mm discharge pipe 100 m long, static head 27.00 m, η = 75%) computes Total Dynamic Head (TDH) = 44.612 m, Hydraulic Power = 2.18 kW, Brake Power = 2.91 kW, and NPSHa = 7.230 m.
assumptions: Steady-state incompressible Newtonian fluid flow in full circular pipes with constant temperature and fluid properties.
Darcy-Weisbach major head loss using Swamee-Jain / Colebrook-White friction factor and user-specified pipe absolute roughness.
Minor losses summed via resistance coefficient K factors for elbows, valves, strainers, entrance, and exit fittings.
NPSHa evaluated at pump centerline using barometric/vessel surface pressure minus vapor pressure, static lift, and suction losses.
limits: Not valid for non-Newtonian slurries, high-viscosity laminar pastes outside Reynolds transition range, or flashing/two-phase suction lines.
Does not generate pump characteristic H-Q curves or check parallel/series pump interaction stability.
API 610 hydrocarbon service requires an additional NPSHa/NPSHr margin (typically >= 1.0 m or ratio >= 1.2) against vendor pump data.
pump-head.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

orifice-plate.standard_clause: ISO 5167-2:2003 (Reader–Harris/Gallagher discharge coefficient & compressible expansibility factor ε); API MPMS Ch. 14.3 (AGA Report No. 3)
orifice-plate.worked_example: Default on-page metric liquid case (pipe D = 100.0 mm, orifice d = 50.0 mm, ΔP = 1000.0 Pa, Cd = 0.61, ρ = 1000.0 kg/m³, μ = 0.001 Pa·s) computes volumetric flow Qv = 1.7494×10⁻³ m³/s (~0.002 m³/s), mass flow Qm = 1.7494 kg/s, β = 0.5000, and Re = 2.227×10⁴.
assumptions: Concentric, square-edged thin orifice plate in a full, clean circular conduit with steady, non-pulsating flow.
User-entered or standard-correlated discharge coefficient Cd paired with upstream static fluid density and viscosity.
Incompressible flow (ε = 1.0) for liquids; ideal-gas isentropic compressibility correction for gases.
limits: ISO 5167-2 geometric validity: 0.10 <= β <= 0.75, 50 mm <= D <= 1000 mm, orifice bore d >= 12.5 mm, and minimum pipe Re_D >= 5,000.
Requires adequate straight upstream and downstream pipe lengths (10D–44D upstream depending on β and fittings) for swirl-free velocity profile.
Manual override of Cd outside standard tapping correlations shifts result accuracy outside ISO 5167 uncertainty bounds.
orifice-plate.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

voltage-drop.standard_clause: IEC 60364-5-52 Annex G; NEC 210.19 / 215.2 & Ch. 9 Table 9 (AC impedance & voltage drop); IEEE 141 (Red Book); BS 7671
voltage-drop.worked_example: Default on-page 400 V three-phase LV case (I = 100 A, pf = 0.85, L = 100 m, 35 mm² Cu in PVC conduit at 70 °C) computes voltage drop = 9.98 V (2.49%), load voltage = 390.0 V, effective impedance Z_eff = 0.5761 Ω/km, and max run length at 5% drop = 200 m.
assumptions: Steady-state fundamental frequency phasor drop approximated as Z_eff = R(T_op) cos(φ) + X sin(φ).
Conductor DC/AC resistance linearly adjusted from 20 °C reference to specified operating temperature (cu/al temperature coefficient).
Balanced three-phase (√3 factor) or single-phase / DC (2× loop factor) feeder loading with uniform cable cross-section.
limits: Does not model transient motor starting inrush voltage dips or harmonic-frequency impedance magnification.
Assumes receiving-end power factor equals nominal load power factor without longitudinal shunt capacitance charging currents (long MV lines).
NEC/IEC recommended limits (3% branch circuit / 5% total feeder+branch) are design targets requiring local code verification.
voltage-drop.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

short-circuit.standard_clause: IEC 60909-0 (equivalent voltage source factor c, initial symmetrical current Ik", and peak factor κ / ip); ANSI/IEEE C37; IEEE 1584-2018
short-circuit.worked_example: Default on-page 415 V three-phase bolted fault case (500 MVA utility X/R = 15, 1000 kVA transformer Z = 5.75% X/R = 6, 2×240 mm² 20 m cable feeder, 100 kW motor Xd" = 0.2) computes symmetrical RMS current = 22.41 kA, peak making current = 48.33 kA, X/R = 4.52, and total impedance Z1 = 0.0646 pu.
assumptions: Equivalenced three-phase symmetrical components converted to a common per-unit MVA base per IEC 60909 methodology.
Pre-fault system voltage modeled using IEC 60909 voltage factor c; utility source, step-down transformer, feeder, and motor lumped at fault bus.
Initial symmetrical short-circuit current (Ik") and peak making current (ip) computed using equivalent fault bus X/R ratio.
limits: Valid for single-bus radial system topology (utility + single transformer + feeder + aggregated motor bank); meshed networks require full Z-bus solver.
Bolted fault assumption excludes arc impedance reductions; single-line-to-ground faults depend strongly on entered transformer NGR ohm value.
Does not compute time-varying breaking current (Ib) decay beyond initial subtransient period without generator decrement curves.
short-circuit.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

grounding.standard_clause: IEEE Std 80 (Dwight single-rod resistance and tolerable Ep/Es step & touch voltage criteria); IEC 60364; IEEE 81; NEC 250.52
grounding.worked_example: Default on-page single-layer soil industrial rod case (ρ = 100 Ω·m, L = 3.0 m, d = 16 mm, N = 1 copper rod, If = 5000 A, t = 0.2 s) computes single and total earth resistance Rtotal = 33.493 Ω.
assumptions: Homogeneous isotropic single-layer (or two-layer) soil resistivity model measured via Wenner four-pin testing.
Vertical driven rod resistance evaluated via Dwight's formula; parallel rod efficiency accounts for mutual spacing interference.
Surface crushed-rock layer factor Cs applied to tolerable step and touch body-current limits for 50 kg / 70 kg person models.
limits: Analytical rod/grid approximations omit complex soil stratification, nearby buried metallic piping, and seasonal frost/drought moisture swings.
Grid conductor sizing assumes uniform thermal fault current distribution without dynamic soil breakdown or ionization.
Final substation earth grid safety must be verified with IEEE 81 fall-of-potential and step/touch field measurements post-installation.
grounding.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience

pressurereliefvalve.standard_clause: API Std 520 Part I (critical/subcritical gas, Napier steam & viscous liquid orifice sizing equations); API Std 526; API Std 521; ASME Section VIII; ISO 4126
pressurereliefvalve.worked_example: Default on-page conventional gas relief case (W = 50,000 lb/hr, Pset = 100 psig, 10% overpressure, Pb = 5 psig, MW = 28.97, T = 150 °F, k = 1.40, Z = 1.0, Kd = 0.975) computes required area A_req = 5.2984 in² (P1 = 124.7 psia) and selects API Orifice 'P' (effective area 6.38 in², 4" × 6" flanges).
assumptions: Single-phase relieving fluid (gas/vapor, dry saturated steam via Napier + superheat/backpressure factors, or incompressible liquid).
Constant isentropic exponent k and compressibility Z evaluated at relieving pressure P1 and temperature T1.
Effective discharge coefficient Kd and backpressure/rupture-disc factors (Kb, Kc) applied per selected spring-loaded, balanced bellows, or pilot valve type.
limits: Conventional spring-loaded PRVs limited to <= 10% superimposed/built-up backpressure of set pressure (use balanced bellows up to 50% or pilot-operated).
Does not perform two-phase flashing HEM Omega-method sizing; user must apply two-phase specialized methods for flashing mixtures.
API 526 orifice area selection stops at standard letter orifices 'D' through 'T' (0.110 in² to 26.0 in²); inlet line pressure drop must stay <= 3% of set pressure.
pressurereliefvalve.reviewer: Anil Sharma, Engineering Expert, 25+ yrs industrial experience
